hostExtensions.name: dsh-loopx-plugin
hostExtensions.activation: The official loopx skill activates the native driver in its exact session.
hostExtensions.adaptation: Image-build installation, read-only bootstrap, and a digest-bound DSH tool-result envelope compatibility patch; goal state and scheduling remain the upstream implementation.
hostExtensions.recordAuthority: LoopX owns workspace goal state. EviMed records automated turns and usage; research memory remains in the control plane.

hostExtensions.name: @openviking/dsh-memory-plugin
hostExtensions.switch: OPEN_SCIENCE_OV_NATIVE_MEMORY_ENABLED and the account's memory engine, which reach the runtime as EVIMED_MEMORY_GATEWAY_URL (empty for every account not on the native engine)
hostExtensions.activation: The socket's patch enables the row only when that address is set, and points it at the loopback row evimed-memory-bridge, which forwards to the control plane's memory gateway with the workload token of the moment and answers only its own plugin's local key.
hostExtensions.adaptation: None: the archive is digest-checked when fetched and the installed files are compared with it byte for byte (deploy/runtime-dsh/install-openviking-plugin.mjs). Configured, not edited: autoRecall, captureToolResults, workspacePeer and skillCatalog off, skipSubagentSessions on, the default commit threshold, no key and no identity in the row; the same settings are stated as the plugin's environment so a workspace file cannot overrule them.
hostExtensions.recordAuthority: OpenViking keeps a native account's long-term memory; the control plane's memory gateway fixes identity, routes, the five memory tools and who is learned from. The platform's own recall and note tools stand aside for such an account.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-cite
communityToolBundles.registration: upstream buildCiteTools with managed fetch; original apply replaced
communityToolBundles.readiness: Installed is not runtime-ready: cite_health and a successful DOI lookup must pass with the current model gateway token.
communityToolBundles.evidence: Booted against dsh@0.1.7-rc.2 from a seeded host profile on 2026-09-28 with its host row enabled: the composition activated with no pending entry, and cite_lookup, cite_format, cite_bibtex, cite_check and cite_health were in the tool list of every root model request the kernel sent (mock model upstream; outputs/2026-09-28-dsh-upgrade/evidence).

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-plugin-academic-writing
communityToolBundles.reason: Installs and boots on the pinned kernel (the earlier peer refusal named @deepseek-ai/dsh-fs, a package the 0.1.7 kernel no longer ships, so nothing refuses it now). Not taken: its row injects a persona section into every system prompt by default (personaSection: true), it adds one tool schema to every first request, and the manuscript-support capability already covers the same ground; no measured gain over it.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-plugin-translation
communityToolBundles.reason: Installs and boots on the pinned kernel (same peer note as academic-writing). Not taken: persona section injected into every system prompt by default, one more tool schema in every first request, and its consistency checks are unmeasured against the model's own translation; revisit with a paired evaluation.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-plugin-writing-guard
communityToolBundles.reason: Install refused by the profile's build policy: its postinstall (scripts/install-extras.mjs) copies a skill and a Python module into $DSH_HOME/skills and $DSH_HOME/plugins at install time. The runtime profile is sealed and read-only and nothing is installed during a turn, so a postinstall-installed file set cannot exist there; allowBuilds stays deny-by-default.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-univer-office
communityToolBundles.reason: Installs and boots on the pinned kernel (peers admit 0.1.7-rc.1). Not taken: 213 MB added to the image (201 MB of viewer assets); pulls closed-source native bindings (@univerjs-pro/exchange-node-binding, engine-formula-rust-binding, cli-assets) that carry no licence field, so the plugin's Apache-2.0 does not cover what it runs; product telemetry is on by default (config telemetry: true); documents live in its own libsql worktree store and reach the user through a browser viewer with approve-or-discard cards, which the hosted frame does not mount and which would be a new approval step.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-office-tools
communityToolBundles.reason: Installs and boots. Not taken: capability. word_update only appends, excel_update replaces sheets or writes cells, ppt_* only creates and reads, and PPT images are linked, not embedded (its write channel is UTF-8 text); nothing edits one clause in place or restructures a deck. Its declared compatibility ends at 0.1.5-rc.2 and 0.2.0-rc.1. python-docx, python-pptx and openpyxl, with the office skills' helpers, cover read, edit and create.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-office
communityToolBundles.reason: Installs and boots, but it is another product with a colliding name: an agent-fleet dashboard (sprite office over workspaces, sessions, token use, Feishu messages, agent mail, meetings through lark-cli). It registers no document tools and reads other sessions' data, which the tenancy boundary does not allow a runtime to do.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-zagens-office
communityToolBundles.reason: Not on the registry: a GitHub-only package whose four tools (office_schema, office_write, office_edit, office_read) shell out to a local zagens-office CLI the image does not carry. A pin needs a registry artifact with an integrity digest, and an external executable of unknown provenance is not something the image builds in.

communityToolBundles.name: @zhtx2026/dsh-pdf
communityToolBundles.reason: Installs and boots (the npm package named dsh-pdf is another author's). Not taken: pdf_info, pdf_extract_text and pdf_render_page are covered by pdfplumber and the kit's PDFium page renderer, which the pdf skill already drives; it would add pdfjs-dist (37 MB) and a native canvas binding (30 MB per architecture) and three tool schemas to every first request.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-drawio
communityToolBundles.reason: Install refused by the kernel: "Plugin dsh-drawio@0.1.0 is incompatible with dsh 0.1.7-rc.2" - it pins @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools, dsh-workspace, dsh-attachment and dsh-session to exactly 0.1.0-rc.6. It would also add 92 MB and embed the diagrams.net editor; the repository's licence reads NOASSERTION while the package says Apache-2.0.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-diagram
communityToolBundles.reason: Installs and boots, and declares 0.1.7-rc.2 compatible. Not taken: it is a browser surface (an Excalidraw canvas with React 18 and 17 peer dependencies, eight of them client modules) that the headless try-install lane cannot qualify, 25 MB, and the hosted frame serves only client bundles recorded with a deployment switch. Mermaid already draws diagrams in replies; revisit when a client bundle can be tried in the hosted frame.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-excel-chat
communityToolBundles.reason: Installs and boots ("ready: 25 tools registered"). Not taken: 25 tool schemas in every first request, nine of which (chart, pivot and PDF export, visual review) need Windows with a local Excel; its goal mode plans with a model call inside the tool. Formula health, recalculation and error cells are covered by xlsx_tool and the kit's recalculate.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-data-insight
communityToolBundles.reason: Installs and boots; a 128 KB instruction-only skill (data-insight-runbook) with a CSV profiling script. Not taken without a measured gain: it overlaps exploratory-data-analysis and dataset-research-scoping, and principle 11 asks for a paired run before a second skill for the same request is mounted.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-ppt
communityToolBundles.reason: The plugin form of the community skill already vendored (decision: keep the skill). Installs and boots with seven ppt_* tools; its edit, reorder and undo work on its own project files and a settings-page client, and its peer pins @deepseek-ai/libreoffice-kit to exactly 0.1.5 while the kernel carries 0.1.1. Decks that already exist are restructured with the office pptx skill.

communityToolBundles.name: dsh-cowork
communityToolBundles.reason: Descriptor and isolated-tool pipeline exist and stay (activation not-wired, qualification unverified). Not wired: doc_write creates xlsx and ipynb only and never edits, doc_read of docx and pdf is covered in the run's own sandbox, and every call costs a disposable container. The admission code is no longer written for this repository (isolatedToolRowIsAdmitted); a tool is admitted by its descriptor's digest, coordinate and permission profile.

communityClientBundles.name: dsh-annotation
communityClientBundles.what: Select a passage in a reply, annotate it, and the annotations travel with the next message as plain text prepended to the user turn. Client-side only: it registers no tools and reaches no network.
communityClientBundles.evidence: Booted against dsh@0.1.5-rc.2 in the production runtime image on 2026-09-15 (try-install.json), and again on 2026-09-20 from a seeded host profile, where its client was served in the kernel's plugin bundle. Its peer is the bare `cordis` package, pinned exactly because pnpm would otherwise install whatever the range resolves to on the build day. The image build smoke boots it on every full build. On 2026-09-28 it was booted against dsh@0.1.7-rc.2 from a seeded host profile and its client was served in the kernel's plugin bundle, loading without a console error in the hosted frame.

communityClientBundles.name: dsh-mermaid
communityClientBundles.what: Renders fenced Mermaid diagrams in replies (PRISMA flow, study-selection trees) with a diagram/code toggle. Client-side only; the counts in a diagram still have to come from the screening ledger.
communityClientBundles.evidence: Booted against dsh@0.1.5-rc.2 in the production runtime image on 2026-09-15, and again on 2026-09-20 from a seeded host profile, where its client was served in the kernel's plugin bundle. The 2026-09-15 source scan's net/proc/fsWrite hits were read one by one: coincidental substrings in the browser-side Mermaid+KaTeX build and the package's own CLI, not the plugin (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-24-dsh-ecosystem-adoption-shortlist.md). On 2026-09-28 it was booted against dsh@0.1.7-rc.2 from a seeded host profile and its client was served in the kernel's plugin bundle, loading without a console error in the hosted frame.

updatePolicy: Exact pins are upgraded only through the upstream matrix, dump-config review, image boot smoke and immutable release rollback.
registryContract: Bundles marked installed here are the plugin registry the control plane serves, capped by APPLY_PATH_PLUGIN_IDS in apps/server/src/pluginService.mjs to the ids its apply path can carry; anything else is unconfigurable by name, and marking a bundle installed before that path carries it is refused rather than served. npmPackage is the coordinate the runtime image installs from, and is what the nightly matrix polls for availability; a bundle without one is never looked up, so its availability stays unknown rather than guessed.
clientBundleContract: communityClientBundles are client-side bundles with no tools and no settings. The runtime image installs each at the recorded version (deps-version.json and the Dockerfiles carry the same value; a test holds them equal), and each is turned off deployment-wide by its own switch, which the control plane's profile patch renders as `disabled: true` on the bundle's row. They are not per-project plugins: the plugin registry reads communityToolBundles only.

evimed-duplicate-lines.readiness: The hosted runtime sets this switch on unless explicitly disabled. Unset standalone profiles stay off. Actual native DSH retained one command log line plus the exact repetition count before truncation, and preserved all scientific CSV rows.

kernelNativeOffice.name: @deepseek-ai/libreoffice-kit
kernelNativeOffice.how: Part of the DSH kernel's own closure (installed with the kernel at the pin, under its --before cutoff and closure check), so no new pin and no system LibreOffice in the image. runtime/skills/office/shared/office_kit.py finds its CLI (global kernel install, sealed profile, or EVIMED_LIBREOFFICE_KIT_CLI) and drives convert, recalculate and render; the office skills' helpers call it.
kernelNativeOffice.evidence: shared/test_office_flows.py: docx to PDF keeps the contract at three pages, a 5,000-row workbook recalculates and its formulas stay formulas, a dark deck renders dark, a PDF page renders to PNG. install-runtime.sh office-smoke runs the suite with EVIMED_OFFICE_REQUIRE_KIT=1, so an image without the kit fails its build.

kernelNativeOffice.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-office
kernelNativeOffice.how: Its read-only structural checker (assets/scripts/check_office.py, standard library only) is what `office_kit.py check` runs. Its three skill bodies (office-docx, office-pptx, office-xlsx) are not mounted: they would sit beside the office pack's docx, pptx and xlsx under different names for the same requests, depend on the load_workspace_dependencies tool this composition does not mount, and do not cover restructuring a deck or editing one clause byte-stably. To mount them anyway, the composition row is `- name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-office'` (WP-PROMPT's composition files).
